title: What is an eID-native identity platform? | Identity Infrastructure Explained
summary: An eID-native identity platform puts eIDs, bank IDs and digital wallets first, with documents as fallback. What it is and what the EU AMLR changes.
body_markdown:
*The category explained: 3 generations of identity, and one infrastructure that orchestrates them.*


An eID-native identity platform is identity infrastructure built around government electronic IDs (eIDs), bank IDs and digital identity wallets as the primary way to identify, onboard and authenticate customers. In the EU, the shift is driven by the Anti-Money Laundering Regulation (AMLR), which applies from 10 July 2027, and by AMLA's draft standards on customer due diligence, under which remote verification is expected to use electronic identification, including the EUDI Wallet, wherever possible. Document and selfie checks stay available as a fallback where no eID exists. One integration connects all of these methods and routes each customer to the most suitable one available.


*Written by Jarek Sygitowicz (Co-founder and Chief Strategy Officer), Authologic.*
